I’ll check the saved baseline results and confirm the fixed core build was restored, then complete the caller changes and verification for this phase. I’ll use the SASE memory, repository, artifact, monitor, and finalization workflows as required.


The baseline measurements finished, and the fixed core checkout and extension were restored to `6d11122e`. The monitor failed during artifact publication because detached monitors lack agent identity; I’m publishing the saved results from this turn before reviewing them.


The caller audit found three historical workarounds: the ownership lookup’s 1-second timeout, stage triage’s 2-second timeout, and detach tests’ 5-second reads with busy-error retries. I’ll replace those with the core default while preserving settlement polling deadlines, interactive budgets, and the executor’s remaining-deadline calculations.


The stage-triage test exposed an important distinction: it deliberately holds a writer for 600 ms, beyond the core’s 250 ms default. I’ll retain its bounded 2-second allowance and move the test’s lock holder into a separate process to honor SQLite ownership. The ownership lookup and detach read workarounds can still be removed.


All ten selected nodes passed the unchanged baseline: each completed 10 serial and 20 loaded runs, with all eight requested workers granted. That gives us a clean comparison, but no natural reproduction. I’ll keep those rates separate from the controlled lock tests used to demonstrate the fix.


The caller changes and 100 focused contract checks pass. Defaults now delegate to Rust, and explicit budgets still pass through. The core pin advanced to `6d11122e`; ancestry and build-provenance checks confirm it includes the fix and does not regress the previous pin.


Ordinary writer locks and short exclusive locks behave correctly on both builds, so they don’t demonstrate the regression. I’m now testing the WAL shared-memory initialization window, where SQLite may return busy before its normal timeout can help. No flake entries have been retired.


The last-close probe now demonstrates the failure: pausing the old SQLite cleanup while it held the database’s exclusive lock caused `show` to fail 10/10 times at about 251 ms. With the fixed core, cleanup took no such lock and all 10 reads passed in under 2 ms. The delay was injected; these are controlled results, separate from the natural stress runs.


The syscall traces confirm the sequence: the old build releases the WAL writer lock, then takes an exclusive database lock to checkpoint and remove WAL files. The fixed build skips that cleanup lock. I’m preparing the monitored after-run with the same natural stress protocol, complete affected test files, and controlled per-node tests to support selective flake retirement.


The baseline logs, lock traces, build hashes, and reusable probes are saved as audited evidence. I’m handing the longer verification batch to SASE’s monitor. Its continuation will review per-node results, retire only supported flake entries, run the required health and guarded checks, and close only `sase-1ou.2.1.2`.
